items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with moments of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

It is with great sadness that we share the heartbreaking news that City Staff member Steve Bairos passed away on April 1, 2026, surrounded by the love of his family, after a battle with cancer. Steve was a good friend and colleague and was a devoted and loving father to his daughters Maizie and Zoë. He was an incredible partner to Jessica.

Jessica Bairos shared the following with us: "We want to sincerely thank everyone at the City of Waterloo for the kindness, compassion, and unwavering support you showed him throughout his journey. It meant the world to him. Stephen was so proud and honoured to work for the City of Waterloo, and he spoke so highly of the people he worked with—it truly meant so much to him to be part of that community." Steve, as a person and on his treatment journey, was a positive force in City Utilities after joining the City in 2019 as a Wastewater Operator. He split his time between the Wastewater Operations Section, where he enjoyed "...dressing up in hazmat and rodding clean outs, even on [his] spare time....", and the Water Operations Section, as Water Operator, where he gained notoriety through his handling of old school paper document processing.
Steve will be greatly missed by everyone who had the pleasure of experiencing his positive outlook, humour, and incredible strength. The booster juice will be remembered.

CAO Tim Anderson and I attended Steve’s visitation last Thursday, and staff colleagues attended his funeral on Friday. Flags at all City facilities have been lowered since learning of Steve’s death and will remain lowered until tomorrow.
We extend our sincerest condolences to Steve’s family, friends, and co-workers.

items.title: Adoption and approval of Sugarbush
notes: South Land Use documents (OPA, ZBA
and Urban Design Guidelines)
Report No.: IPPW2026-018
Prepared By: Brenna MacKinnon
Ward No.: Ward 6 – Central Columbia

Brenna MacKinnon gave a presentation outlining the background of the Sugarbush South project, including the key themes heard during the public engagement. Richard Kelly-Ruetz, GSP Group continued the presentation detailing the key recommendations for the project, including the redesignation of the neighbourhood to allow for “missing middle housing”. Evelyn Thomas, GSP Group concluded the presentation with information on the new Urban Design Guidelines. Brenna MacKinnon, Joel Cotter, Adam Lauder, Robin Milne and Beth Maxwell responded to questions of Council.
Richard Kelly-Ruetz also responded to questions of Council.
Elizabeth Parsons, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the trees in the neighbourhood, and the importance of keeping old trees. Elizabeth Parsons then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Vasic noted that the Lincoln Heights Easter Party took place on Saturday, April 11 at the Moses Springer Community Centre, but she was unable to attend. She also noted that Mayor McCabe attended the event. Councillor Vasic further shared that lighting will be installed along the Moses Springer trail this year.
Mayor McCabe added that it was a great event and expressed appreciation to the Neighbourhood Association for organizing it, as well as to Community Services staff for providing tents and games.

Councillor Wright mentioned that the Uptown Egg Hunt took place on Saturday, April 11 and was well attended by families and children, with 50 Uptown businesses participating. She also shared that Waterloo hosted the AAA U13 boys’ hockey provincials, and that some of the players took part in the festivities. Councillor Wright thanked staff for their support in hosting the tournament at the Waterloo Memorial Recreation Complex.

Mayor McCabe added that the Waterloo Wolves placed fourth, losing the bronze medal game. She also shared that the Toronto Marlboros, who had not lost a game since October, were defeated in the final by the Quinte Red Devils. She expressed appreciation for the hard work of staff involved in the tournament.

Mayor McCabe also noted that preparations were underway for Council for a Day on Thursday, April 16. She shared that Service Centre staff look forward to the event each year, which concludes with a mock Council meeting in Council Chambers. She added that she was also looking forward to the State of the City on Thursday and to spending time with Waterloo students participating in the program.
